FACT CHECK: No, Malabon congressman Oreta did not wish for Sara Duterte’s death
FACT CHECK: Escudero didn’t say prosecution ‘fabricated’ allegations vs VP Sara

blocks.text: – Angelee Kaye Abelinde/Rappler.com
Angelee Kaye Abelinde is a student journalist based in Naga City, and an alumna of Rappler’s Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship 2024.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

articles.title: 'Blood is on our hands': Haitian honour student's death sparks outcry over ICE ankle monitors
articles.summary: Pierre Damas Bel fled Haiti and came to the U.S. with a dream of becoming a neurosurgeon. But after U.S. immigration authorities fitted the 20-year-old university student with an ankle monitor, he…

image.caption: Pierre Damas Bel was an aspiring doctor and neuroscience student at Wright State University. After U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement fitted him with an ankle monitor in July, he walked into highway traffic in what his family believes was a suicide. (pierre_d_bel_7/Instagram)

blocks.text: Warning: This story contains descriptions of suicide.
Decorated with academic and athletic awards, Pierre Damas Bel was well on his way to fulfilling his dream of becoming a neurosurgeon.

Described by teachers as a "student of the highest calibre" and a "deeply dedicated" member of his community, Bel was an honour student, captain of the varsity soccer team and volunteer at a food bank in Springfield, Ohio.
But this summer, Bel lost the protected immigration status that allowed him to legally live in the U.S. after fleeing the ongoing instability in Haiti in 2024.

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) fitted the 20-year-old Wright State University student with an ankle monitor in late July as an "alternative to detention." But the device prevented him from playing soccer, and he reportedly began to be bullied by classmates and felt he was "treated like an animal."
"I came here to study, to build my future … not to be treated like [a] criminal," he wrote in a post.

Bel was one of about 350,000 Haitians living and working in the U.S. who lost temporary protected status (TPS) after a U.S. Supreme Court ruling allowed the Trump administration to revoke the humanitarian protection.
Homeland Security's deportation campaign began immediately.
"Those with terminated TPS are in our nation illegally," it posted alongside a video showing Haitian migrants in chains, escorted onto a repatriation flight on Aug. 27.

Once a lieutenant in his high school's Junior Reserve Officers' Training Corps (JROTC) program and described as a "natural leader" who would become a "great American," Bel was the only one in the Wright State ROTC program not to be given a uniform because of the monitor, his father says.
The following Monday, Bel walked into traffic on a nearby highway and was struck by a semi-truck, according to Ohio State Highway Patrol.
He died on the scene. His family believes it was a suicide.
'100% preventable'
In the following days, memorials were held in his honour in Ohio and across the U.S., including New York City. Many held ICE's immigration crackdown responsible for his death.
"Racist anti-Haitian campaign murdered Pierre Damas Bel," one woman's sign in New York read.
Asked to respond to advocates' allegations that the shame of the ankle monitor drove Bel to suicide, ICE told CBC any attempts to blame the agency for his death are false.
"No one is required to stay in the United States illegally and wear a GPS monitor," the agency wrote, adding that self-deportation is an option.
But Yola Lamarre, a friend of Bel, says ICE's response oversimplifies Bel's mental health crisis and blames the young man for his own death.
"We have to be honest in where blood is on our hands," she told CBC News.
Lamarre, who saw Bel as a little brother, said his death was "100 per cent preventable" if he had been treated more humanely.
"He told me how he would try to wear a certain wardrobe to hide the ankle monitor," she said.
"He just wanted belonging. He just wanted acceptance."

items: At least 47 people killed in violent weekend attacks in Haiti, UN says
Who can protect Haiti? An inside look at a country trying to repel violent gangs

blocks.text: Haitians were granted TPS after the 2010 earthquake that killed more than 300,000 people in the Caribbean country. Other crises, including cholera outbreaks, Hurricane Sandy and the assassination of Haitian President Jovenel Moïse, prompted further extensions.

After failed attempts to end Haiti's TPS in Trump's first term, the Department of Homeland Security announced in June 2025 it was ending it, saying the situation had "improved enough that it is safe for Haitian citizens to return home." Meanwhile, the U.S. State Department tells its citizens not to travel to Haiti due to the risk of "crime, kidnapping, terrorism, unrest and limited health care."

The ankle monitoring program Bel was subjected to appears to be part of a larger strategy by ICE to "make life so miserable" that Haitians will self-deport, said Carl Ruby, senior pastor at Central Christian Church in Springfield, Ohio, a city where at least 10,000 of its roughly 60,000 residents are Haitian.
"They're afraid to go outside of their homes," said Ruby, whose church saw its Haitian attendance plummet from about 50 people to two.
Residents 'shackled'
Ruby said hundreds of Springfield residents — including teenagers, elderly and pregnant people — have been "shackled" with ankle monitors, often leading to deep shame and social isolation.
"Their old friends start to pull back from them because they're afraid that if they're with a person who has an ankle monitor, that they might be apprehended."
Critics like Ohio Democratic congressman Greg Landsman say the electronic monitoring program also unfairly humiliates law-abiding migrants.
"They aren't criminals," wrote Landsman. "It's all so wrong and cruel to pick on anybody, especially a group this vulnerable."
Canadian immigration 'very difficult' for Haitians in U.S., says advocate
Viles Dorsainvil, executive director of the Haitian Support Center in Springfield, said his community members are caught in a catch-22: no longer safe in the U.S., they also have nowhere to go.
"There is no country that is willing to welcome us," said Dorsainvil, who lost TPS himself. "We cannot go to work. We live in fear and anxiety on a daily basis."
The end of TPS has had a chilling effect across the wider Haitian diaspora in the U.S.

items: Why is Trump so focused on Haiti?
Haitians in the U.S. brace for deportation as Trump ends their protected status

blocks.text: At a Springfield strip mall, once a hub of economic activity with several Haitian-owned businesses, storefronts were locked or shuttered altogether when CBC visited last week.
One store employee, who asked not to be identified because of his immigration status, described the situation as a "catastrophe."
"There are many people who don't have enough to eat, who are sick, who don't have access to medical care … and no way to get to a doctor," the asylum seeker told CBC in French.
'There's no life for them,' restauranteur says of Haitians who lost protected status
Other businesses are struggling to pay their bills.

Claucia Dossous, a Haitian American who runs T-Co Islands Restaurant in Columbus, Ohio, said ending TPS has "broken everybody's life" after Haitians who frequented her restaurant were forced out of work.
"I pay for the price, too."
Looking to Canada
The climate of fear has led some Haitians to try moving to Canada.

More Haitian nationals file for asylum at the land border than any other country so far this year, according to the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA). Figures from the Immigration and Refugee Board show that more than 27,000 Haitians are awaiting decisions — about 1/10th of all pending asylum claims.
Haitian American activist Guerline Jozef wants Canada to open more humanitarian pathways for Haitians who no longer feel safe in their country.

"We find ourselves in a place where we cannot leave, we cannot stay. And the only option they are giving them is to be kidnapped and be deported to the same place that they have fled," said Jozef, executive director of the Haitian Bridge Alliance in San Diego, Calif.
Canada returning Haitian asylum seekers to U.S. immigration authorities, says activist
Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada told CBC it "cannot speculate on future policy decisions" but highlighted temporary measures for Haitian nationals in place until October.
But for those outside Canada, those measures are only available to family members of Canadian citizens and permanent residents.
Ruby described the case of one family who was a part of their congregation who survived several kidnapping attempts in Haiti.
Haitian student in Ohio ended his life over 'humiliating' ICE ankle monitor, family believes
Because one of them had a sister in Canada, they were able to join her. The day they arrived in Canada, they received letters from ICE telling them their TPS was over and to self-deport.
"They got out just in time," he said. "But that option just isn't available to very many people."
Instead, Jozef said many of the people who try to flee the U.S. into Canada are turned away.

Under the Safe Third Country Agreement, refugees who first arrive in the U.S. are barred from seeking asylum in Canada, barring certain exceptions. More than 1,100 asylum seekers were returned to U.S. immigration authorities under this agreement so far this year, according to the CBSA.
Montreal migrant advocate Frantz André said the agreement now effectively allows for "deportation by proxy" when Canadian agents turn back Haitian migrants knowing they will be deported by the U.S.
"The United States is no longer a safe country for hundreds of thousands of people," he said. "People are in despair."

articles.title: Millions of fish tested Canada's largest nuclear plant. The incident points to a growing climate risk
articles.summary: A freak fish event that 'challenged reactor safety' at Canada's largest nuclear plant shows why the nuclear energy governments are relying on to fight climate change must also become more resilient…

image.caption: Gizzard shad are sensitive to cold water and can suffer from cold shock when temperatures plunge. In winter, they can congregate around warmer water created by industrial and sewage discharges, including the thermal discharge fro the Bruce Nuclear Generating Station. (United States Fish and Wildlife

blocks.text: Almost two years after a freak fish event at Canada's largest nuclear power plant "challenged reactor safety," newly obtained documents show how extraordinary the event was — as experts warn unusual ecological conditions are becoming a growing challenge for nuclear plants around the world.

In February 2025, millions of gizzard shad overwhelmed cooling systems at Bruce Nuclear Generating Station near Tiverton, Ont., shutting down one reactor, reducing power at another and leaving dead fish washing ashore along Lake Huron for days.

CBC News obtained more than 1,200 pages of federal and provincial records that reveal how an environmental phenomenon involving a small, cold-sensitive fish tested Canada's largest nuclear power plant in ways its operators had not anticipated.
Bruce Power, the private company that operates the plant, declined a broadcast interview. The company later provided a written statement, but did not answer CBC News's specific questions.
Dead fish 'challenged reactor safety'

Bruce Power's own root-cause investigation concluded the plant had encountered "a novel environmental event." Canada's nuclear regulator described an "uncharacterized and unanticipated volume of gizzard shad" — enough to overwhelm defences meant to keep fish out of the plant's cooling water system.
Another company investigation concluded in June 2025 that the two fish runs, on Feb. 1 and Feb. 13, "challenged reactor safety."

David Novog, a professor at McMaster University and Canada Research Chair in Nuclear Safety, said the phrase has a specific meaning in an industry where plants are protected by multiple layers of defence.

"When we talk about a challenge to reactor safety, what it usually implies is that one of those defences has been reduced in effectiveness or taken offline. And when that happens, nuclear power stations are required to shut down," he said.
There was no risk to reactor safety, in my opinion.- Douglas Boreham, former principal scientist and manager at Bruce Power

Douglas Boreham, a professor of medical sciences at Northern Ontario School of Medicine University who previously worked as a principal scientist and manager at Bruce Power, said the reactors responded as designed when their cooling systems were disrupted.
"Maybe the wording in that document should have been slightly modified to say it was operations that were impacted, but there was no risk to reactor safety, in my opinion," he said.
"There was no safety issue. I mean, it's designed to do that. You shut things down when the system isn't optimal."
Nuclear regulator warned of worst-case scenario
The potential consequences are laid out in an April 2026 report by the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission (CNSC) prepared for the International Atomic Energy Agency.
On Feb. 13, 2025, the mass cold-water fish die-off disrupted cooling systems serving two operating reactors. Bruce Power was forced to shut down Unit 2 and reduce power at Unit 1.

Less than two weeks earlier, on Feb. 1, the fish event affected cooling at Unit 4, which was already shut down for refurbishment. Even after a reactor is shut down, its fuel continues producing heat and must be kept cool.
In formal regulatory correspondence sent to Bruce Power on May 5, 2025, the CNSC warned that "the potential consequences of this event could have resulted in all [four Bruce A] units being shutdown."
8.1 million fish in a single day
The scale of the fish event was enormous.

In a March 2026 report to Fisheries and Oceans Canada, Bruce Power estimated that 8.1 million gizzard shad were in the vicinity of Bruce A on a single day in February 2025 — far exceeding any counts made public at the time.

The report said severe winter conditions, including significant snowfall and a sharp drop in air temperature, pushed water temperatures close to freezing, causing cold shock among the fish. The surviving gizzard shad, a species poorly adapted to cold water, congregated around the warmer water discharged by the nuclear plant.

Ryan Lauzon, a fisheries biologist with nearby Saugeen Ojibway Nation, whose traditional territory includes the Bruce Peninsula and surrounding Lake Huron shoreline, co-authored a report on the 2025 fish kill. He said warmer winters in the years leading up to 2025 — including record-low ice levels in 2024 — may help explain how such a large population developed.
"It is a reasonable hypothesis," he said. "It potentially allowed these fish to develop larger populations" before colder conditions in 2025 left large numbers of fish vulnerable.

Federal records estimate between 3.8 million and 4.95 million gizzard shad became trapped and died at Bruce A between Jan. 30 and March 26, 2025 — several times the previous record of roughly 800,000 set in 1977.

The number was so enormous Bruce Power brought in a crane ito help remove them, according to emails obtained by CBC News from Ontario's Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks. The carcasses were hauled to a landfill.
Reactor shutdown 'a big hit to the grid'
Novog said a reactor shutdown isn't simply a matter of clearing out the dead fish and flicking a switch. Restarting a reactor in Canada would take at least three or four days.
"That's not trivial. Each nuclear station is generating hundreds of megawatts of electricity every hour of the day, so to lose them for multiple days even, is a big hit to the grid," Novog said.

Internal provincial records obtained by CBC News show Ontario's Independent Electricity System Operator said the province's electricity supply was "tight" while Unit 2 remained offline. It assessed a "medium risk" that another Bruce reactor could go offline, but said the grid could remain reliable using electricity imports and other domestic generation.
Nuclear power's climate paradox
What happened at Bruce Power is not the only recent case of environmental conditions disrupting the cooling systems nuclear plants depend on.
Novog said he has seen such events become more common over the course of his career, pointing to events that disrupted nuclear cooling systems in Romania and France.

In the summer of 2026, reactors were forced offline by record-low water levels on the Danube River in Romania. At France's Gravelines nuclear plant, massive influxes of jellyfish clogged cooling systems for two consecutive summers, forcing reactors offline in 2025 and 2026.
Nuclear plants are being forced to adapt to a changing climate, even as governments increasingly rely on them to help fight it.
"It just appears to me that over time, these kind of events have been increasing," Novog said.
'Organizational failure' to adapt

Bruce Power's investigation identified inadequate real-time environmental monitoring and what it called an "organizational failure" to recognize emerging problems associated with changing environmental conditions and make design changes to protect the plant from cooling water blockages.
Since the event, Bruce Power has said it spent nearly $10 million on mitigation measures and research aimed at preventing another mass fish event from disrupting the plant.

In a statement received after CBC News' deadline, Bruce Power said it has strengthened its defences since the fish event and is preparing for emerging risks associated with climate change, acknowledging that "we cannot anticipate every future event."

The measures include new physical barriers to keep fish away from the cooling-water intakes, underwater acoustic deterrents, sonar and video monitoring and an artificial intelligence system intended to provide earlier warning when large numbers of fish approach.
Novog said preventing those disruptions will become increasingly important as nuclear plants are relied upon to provide low-carbon electricity.

"The best solution is to have no fish congregate there and keep the units running and so that's why I think over the years to come, you'll see more on mitigation and prevention measures at Bruce and other stations around the world."

articles.title: Frank Stronach faces sentencing hearing on indecent assault conviction
articles.summary: When his judge-alone trial began in February, Frank Stronach was facing 12 charges related to allegations of sexual assault from seven women. In a sentencing hearing Thursday, the 94-year-old…

image.caption: Earlier this year, Canadian billionaire Frank Stronach was facing 12 charges related to allegations of sexual assault from seven women dating back almost 50 years. A number of those charges were withdrawn. (Alex Lupul/CBC)

blocks.text: Toronto·New

When his judge-alone trial began in February, Frank Stronach was facing 12 charges related to allegations of sexual assault from seven women. In a sentencing hearing Thursday, the 94-year-old businessman could be sentenced on just one of those charges — indecent assault.
Businessman initially faced 12 charges, still faces 2nd trial in Newmarket next year
WARNING: This story refers to sexual assault allegations and may affect those who have experienced​ ​​​sexual violence or know someone affected by it.

When his judge-alone trial began in a Toronto courtroom in February, Canadian billionaire Frank Stronach was facing 12 charges related to allegations of sexual assault from seven women dating back almost 50 years.
But in a sentencing hearing Thursday, the 94-year-old founder of auto-parts giant Magna International could be sentenced on just one of those charges — indecent assault.

On the indecent assault charge, one of the women had told the court that Stronach invited her to a midtown Toronto apartment sometime in the fall of 1977 and, while there, bent her over the arm of a chair, lifted up her skirt and tried to rape her.
Stronach had been charged with attempted rape and indecent assault for that particular incident. But during the course of the trial, the Crown dropped the attempted rape charge.

In her decision, Ontario Superior Court Justice Anne Molloy agreed that much of what the witness described had happened, but also agreed with the Crown's decision to withdraw the attempted rape charge because it was unclear whether Stronach would have been able to penetrate the woman based on her state of dress at the time.

Still, Molloy referred to it as "gross and disgusting conduct," which is why she found him guilty of indecent assault. The offence is a historical charge, having been repealed from the Criminal Code in 1983. That means anyone charged similarly today would face a sexual assault charge.

In June, Molloy also found Stronach guilty of sexual assault related to another woman who said Stronach groped her in his Toronto Harbourfront condo sometime in 1983 or 1984. The woman said she had gone to meet him for dinner to discuss why she had been fired as a waitress at his then restaurant, Rooney's. She said Stronach invited her to his condo, which is where he groped her.

Molloy said she was "completely convinced" by the woman's evidence. Molloy did, however, "with considerable trepidation," describe it as a minor sexual assault, saying that the conduct was at the "low end" of the spectrum of sexual assault.
2nd conviction granted mistrial

However, weeks after the decision, emails were presented in court from the woman's lawyer in a separate civil complaint. Stronach's lawyer Leora Shemesh alleged those emails told a story inconsistent with the woman's testimony in the criminal trial.
Molloy then granted a mistrial on the sexual assault conviction. The Crown is appealing that decision.

Throughout the trial, which lasted more than two months, the Crown withdrew a number of charges following the testimony and cross-examination of some of the complainants, saying there was not sufficient evidence to sustain findings of guilt beyond a reasonable doubt on those particular counts.
By the time Molloy was set to render her decision in June, Stronach was facing five counts related to three women.

items: Crown appealing post-verdict mistrial in Frank Stronach sexual assault conviction
Canadian businessman Frank Stronach found guilty of sexual assault, indecent assault

blocks.text: All of the initial seven complainants, whose allegations span the period between 1977 and 1990, testified in court, offering an emotional account of the sexual offences they say they experienced at the hands of Stronach.
Stronach, who was in court every day but never took the witness box in his own defence, had denied the allegations and pleaded not guilty to all charges.

Meanwhile, Stronach is set to face another trial in Newmarket, Ont., next year. When Stronach was initially arrested in June 2024, he was charged with 18 offences involving 13 complainants. But the case was split into two trials later that year.

If you’re in immediate danger or fear for your safety or that of others around you, please call 911. For support in your area, you can look for crisis lines and local services via the Ending Sexual Violence Association of Canada database. ​​

articles.title: Tories challenge chancellor to rule out tax rises in budget – UK politics live
articles.summary:
The Conservatives want to brand Burnham’s administration as a ‘traditional tax and spend socialist government’

Good morning. With less than six weeks so go until the budget, economics is…

blocks.text: Tories challenge PM to rule out tax cuts in budget, as Badenoch’s attack on TUC Bank of England appointment backfires

Good morning. With less than six weeks so go until the budget, economics is rising up the agenda at Westminster. The Bank of England is announcing its latest interest rate decision later – Graeme Wearden will have all the details on his business live blog – and Andrew Griffith is giving his first major speech since being appointed as shadow chancellor just over two weeks ago.
Not surprisingly, Griffith is urging the chancellor, John Healey, to rule out tax rises in the budget. He has been doing interviews this morning and he told BBC Breakfast:

double quotation markThe taxes or the fear of taxes … are driving really big taxpayers to leave our country for overseas, taking hundreds of millions of pounds of tax revenues that will pay for public services … The thing that they (the government) could do right now is take off the table the fears of ordinary small businesses, the self-employed, who are getting up now, going to work, and allow them to get on with their lives with confidence that the taxes are not going to go up.

The speech will focus on small businesses, and Griffith will announce that he has appointed two advisers – the Tory peer and former MP Craig Mackinlay, a chartered accountant, and Robert Colvile, the outgoing head of the Centre for Policy Studies thinktank – to produce a report for him on cutting red tape for business.

The Tories are keen to present Burnham’s administration as what Andy Haldane would call just another “traditional tax and spend socialist government” and yesterday Kemi Badenoch leapt on what she thought was new evidence to confirm this theory. She posted this on social media.

double quotation markOnly one party has ever rescued the country from trade union control. We’re ready to do so again. If you weren’t sure what kind of Labour government we have, or want to know what’s in store for you and your family finances, the news below is a big clue and it’s not good news 👇
She was responding to a tweet from the Sun saying Paul Nowak has been made a director at the Bank of England.

It was true; he has. There are up to 14 directors on the Bank’s court of directors and Nowak, general secretary of the TUC, has been appointed as one of its non-executive directors. The court is not the body that sets interest rates; it just oversees the Bank’s administration.

But there is nothing very new or surprising (or socialist) about this. Nowak is replacing Frances O’Grady, who was also TUC general secretary. She was made a non-executive director at the Bank under a Tory government. As was her TUC predecessor.

In fact, this has been happening for decades. Rupert Harrison, who was chief of staff to George Osborne when he was chancellor, took to X yesterday to suggest to his Tory colleagues that they keep things in perspective.

double quotation markGot no take on this particular candidate but worth noting that it’s been a tradition to have a trade union representative on the Court of the Bank for decades. Since the War I think.
Here is the agenda for the day.
9.30am: The Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government publishes figures on local government spending.
11am: Andrew Griffith, the shadow chancellor, delivers his speech.
Noon: The Bank of England announces its interest rate decision.

articles.title: Malacañang notes Rodrigo Duterte's 'good condition', acceptance of situation after ICC appearance
articles.summary: Following Rodrigo Duterte"s personal appearance before the International Criminal Court (ICC) at The Hague in the Netherlands on September 16, the Palace on Thursday said the former president…

blocks.text: Published September 17, 2026 3:47pm

Former Philippines president Rodrigo Duterte appears before the International Criminal Court, as the court hears arguments regarding Duterte's health and ability to stand trial, while he faces murder charges related to his war on drugs, in The Hague, Netherlands, September 16 2026. REUTERS/Piroschka van de Wouw/Pool

Following Rodrigo Duterte’s personal appearance before the International Criminal Court (ICC) at The Hague in the Netherlands on September 16, the Palace on Thursday said the former president appeared to be in good condition and appears to have accepted his current legal situation.

Duterte was arrested by Philippine authorities in Pasay City and was handed over to the ICC on March 11, 2025. He was flown via a chartered plane to The Hague where he will be tried for crimes against humanity in relation to his bloody war on drugs while he was mayor of Davao City and President of the Philippines.

“Unang-una sa mga kababayan natin, nakita naman po natin na maganda naman po ang kalagayan ng ating dating pangulo na si dating pangulong Duterte. At nakita naman namin na mukhang accepted naman niya po na magtuloy-tuloy ang hearing sa ICC. So, iyon lamang po,” Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said in a media briefing.
(First of all to our countrymen, we saw that former president Duterte is in good condition. And we saw that it seems that he has accepted that the ICC hearings are continuing.)
The former president physically appeared before ICC judges for the first time for the third status conference of his case.
While he already made an initial appearance at the court in the same month, it was via a videoconference call.
Duterte's family and allies have repeatedly slammed his arrest and subsequent detention.
The Palace has maintained that there was nothing illegal or political about the former president’s turnover to the ICC.

“Interpol asked for help, and we obliged because we have commitments to the Interpol which we have to fulfill. If we don’t do that, they will not – they will no longer help us with other cases involving Filipino fugitives abroad,” President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. said on the night that Duterte was flown to The Hague. —RF, GMA News

articles.title: BuCor says no South Korean drug lord escaped via drone
articles.summary: The Bureau of Corrections has ruled out the possibility of inmates escaping from penal facilities using unmanned aerial vehicles.

blocks.text: September 17, 2026 | 3:43pm
A heavy-duty drone carries an associate of South Korean drug lord Park Wang-yeol over a body of water in footage filmed in March 2026.
Screenshot from JTBC News
MANILA, Philippines — The Bureau of Corrections (BuCor) has ruled out the possibility of inmates escaping from penal facilities using unmanned aerial vehicles.

In a statement on Thursday, Sept. 17, BuCor Director General Gregorio Pio Catapang Jr. addressed media inquiries regarding the alleged drone escapes, following reports from South Korean media alleging that an incarcerated South Korean drug lord, convicted killer Park Wang-yeol, had plotted to fly over prison walls suspended from a heavy-duty drone.
Catapang stressed that correctional facilities under the bureau are strictly designated as no-fly zones.

"All our Operating Prison and Penal Farms are no fly zones, and we have watch towers manned 24/7 which immediately alert our guards if there will be attempts to scape through drones aside from maingay ang drone at equipped naman ang ating facilities ng mga CCTV, so we can detect it at once," Catapang said.

(All of our Operating Prison and Penal Farms are no-fly zones, and we have watchtowers manned 24/7 that immediately alert our guards to any drone-assisted escape attempts. Besides, drones are noisy and our facilities are equipped with CCTVs, so we can detect them at once.)

Catapang emphasized that the audible hum of drone motors, particularly at low altitudes necessary to pick up a payload or passenger, would instantly alert personnel stationed at watchtowers and security perimeters.
In addition, extensive CCTV coverage across prison grounds, buildings, and outer perimeters allows command centers to track and intercept suspicious aerial activity in real time.

While acknowledging growing global concerns over commercially available drones being used to drop contraband or conduct unauthorized surveillance near detention facilities, Catapang maintained that using a drone to execute a physical escape has no chance of success.
"Any drone spotted within or near a facility could be recorded and tracked, enabling authorities to respond quickly," Catapang said.
Meanwhile, in a press conference on Thursday, Department of Justice Undersecretary Ian Dato said the Korean national had already been turned over to South Korean authorities last March.

"Based on the statement from Director General Catapang, no such attempt has been discovered or made while the said Korean national was in its custody. There has never been any attempt, known attempt or any discovered attempt," Dato said.
"We really do not know where that information is coming from," he added.
According to local and international media reports, Park, 47, a notorious South Korean drug lord convicted of murdering three Koreans in the Philippines, did not actually escape.
Instead, he plotted an audacious drone-assisted prison break from a Philippine detention facility in early 2026, but the plan was foiled when test footage surfaced in local media.

articles.title: Ridon issued show cause for impeachment comments
articles.summary: The impeachment court has yet to determine whether the House prosecutor violated Rule 18.

blocks.text: September 17, 2026 | 3:42pm
Rep. Terry Ridon (Bicol Saro Party-list) answers questions from the media in an ambush interview on Tuesday, Sept. 2, 2025.
Philstar.com / Dominique Nicole Flores

MANILA, Philippines — House prosecutor Terry Ridon confirmed on Thursday, September 17, that he is one of the two prosecutors ordered by the Senate impeachment court to explain possible violations of its sub judice rule.

Presiding Officer Chiz Escudero announced yesterday that show-cause orders had been issued to certain members of the House prosecution panel. These orders ask them to explain why they must not be penalized for violating Rule 18.
Escudero did not say which prosecutors received the orders.
The sub judice principle bars parties from publicly commenting on a pending case in ways that could influence its outcome.
"We respect the Senate Impeachment Court, we will answer the Show Cause Order, and we will continue doing our work," Ridon (Bicol Saro) said in a statement.
Ridon said he would be submitting his explanation to the court by the end of the day.

The lawmaker said he would keep leading the prosecution's presentation of the article on unexplained wealth, and continue explaining the trial to the public "in the way they can best understand," in line with the court's rules.
He did not say which of his remarks the court had flagged.

After Escudero's announcement, court spokesperson Reginald Tongol told the media that two prosecution panel members received the show cause orders. One was a private counsel for the House panel, over a September 8 interview, and the other was a lawmaker on the panel, over interviews on September 14 and 15, he said.
Tongol said the court issued the orders on its own initiative and without being raised by the defense.

Under the impeachment court's August ruling, a show-cause order may be issued by the court on its own or on motion of either side, and the respondent must file a verified written answer within 24 hours.
A first violation draws a public reprimand and admonition. Repeat violations carry a P30,000 fine and may bar the violator from speaking, objecting or examining witnesses on the floor.
Escudero had also warned that lawyers who break the rule may be referred to the Supreme Court or the Integrated Bar of the Philippines for disciplinary action.

articles.title: Trump threatens EU with ‘serious tariffs’ after proposal to make Canada first associate member – Europe live
articles.summary:
European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen says such a partnership is for the European Union’s ‘common strength’

US president Donald Trump has threatened the European Union…

blocks.text: Morning opening: Trump threatens Europe, again

blocks.caption: Jakub Krupa

blocks.text: Jakub Krupa

US president Donald Trump has threatened the European Union with “serious tariffs” and a cut to trade after the bloc proposed to make Canada its first ever associate member, calling the idea “laughable”.

Suggesting the move was a “hostile act”, the US president told reporters he could put “very serious tariffs or stop trading with Europe”. He added: “If it’s a good intention, that’s fine. If it’s a bad intention, we’ll put very heavy tariffs on Europe.”

European Commision president Ursula von der Leyen insisted yesterday that “this is not a partnership against anyone else, but for our common strength,” and deputy chief spokesperson Olof Gill repeated this line this morning in response to Trump’s overnight threats.

Canadian prime minister Mark Carney – fresh from watching Everton’s Carabao Cup win over Wolverhampton Wanderers in Liverpool – will address the European parliament late morning. Let’s see if he has anything to say on this.

blocks.caption: Mark Carney and Andy Burnham before the Carabao Cup Third Round match between Everton and Wolverhampton Wanderers at Hill Dickinson Stadium in Liverpool, England. Photograph: Tony McArdle/Everton FC/Getty Images

blocks.text: Separately, our attention is increasingly turning to Germany, where embattled chancellor Friedrich Merz is set to join the campaign trail today in Berlin ahead of this weekend’s two state elections that just could determine his political future.

blocks.caption: German chancellor Friedrich Merz attends a meeting of the German government’s cabinet in Berlin, Germany. Photograph: Filip Singer/EPA

blocks.text: Powerful German state leaders from his party have rallied behind the chancellor as speculation builds that his days in office may be numbered, and he cancelled his trip to the UN general assembly next week.

Our Berlin correspondent Deborah Cole will be joining us just after 11am to answer your questions about Merz’s future, the two state elections, and what’s next for Germany. You can post your questions to her below the line from 9am.
Lots for us to cover today.
It’s Thursday, 17 September 2026, it’s Jakub Krupa here, and this is Europe Live.
Good morning.
Key events

items: 20m agoMorning opening: Trump threatens Europe, again

blocks.caption: Jennifer Rankin

blocks.text: Jennifer Rankin
in Brussels

The 27-member EU has never had an associate membership category, although it has close ties with Norway, Iceland and Switzerland, allowing deep economic integration with these countries, who follow many EU rules.

blocks.caption: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen greeting Canada's prime minister Mark Carney during her annual keynote address to the European Parliament in Strasbourg, eastern France. Photograph: Christophe Licoppe/EUROPEAN UNION/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: It remains to be seen what associate membership means, including for Canada’s relationship with the EU single market. When the UK was negotiating its departure from the bloc and post-Brexit relationship, EU officials repeatedly said there was no status that enabled a foreign country to be half in and half out of the single market.
The phrase itself took EU insiders by surprise since von der Leyen had not used the term when she briefed senior EU diplomats ahead of her speech last Friday.

One EU diplomat said member states were “generally very supportive of ambition” in the EU-Canada relationship, but had been slightly worried in recent weeks that von der Leyen was overpromising on Canada.

“‘Associate membership’ sounds like a nice headline but in reality 10 member states have still not ratified Ceta,” the person said, referring to the EU-Canada trade agreement that was agreed 10 years ago.
A second EU diplomat described associate membership as “an empty phrase”.
Martin Leng at the Brussels Institute for Geopolitics thinktank said a world in flux was “pushing the EU towards far greater flexibility in its relations with third states”.

He said von der Leyen’s speech, with its focus on different sectoral areas of cooperation “points to the ambition and strategic breadth of the associate membership which the parties have in mind but also suggests that, in reality, Canada’s ‘membership’ may consist of ‘plugging in’ to existing programmes and frameworks, such as the European Defence Agency, rather than joining the union in any traditional sense”.

articles.title: After Senate passes bill, will 2026 barangay, SK polls be postponed?
articles.summary: The measure fixes the term of all elected barangay and SK officials to five years and moves the village and youth polls to the second Monday of November starting in 2028

blocks.text: REGISTRATION. Eligible voters line up at a Commission on Elections satellite registration site on the final day of registration to secure their eligibility for the upcoming barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan elections (BSKE), at a mall in Cebu City on May 18, 2026.
Jacqueline Hernandez/Rappler
The measure fixes the term of all elected barangay and SK officials to five years and moves the village and youth polls to the second Monday of November starting in 2028

items: The Senate approved Senate Bill No. 2387, extending the term of barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan officials from four to five years and postponing the elections to November 2028.
The bill, authored by Senator Chiz Escudero, also sets a two-term limit for barangay officials and one term for SK officials, impacting the eligibility of current officials for the 2028 elections.

Opposition from some senators, including Vicente Sotto III, highlights concerns about voter rights and the implications of delaying elections, while election watchdogs warn against the long-term consequences of repeated postponements.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

Over two months before the 2026 barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan elections (BSKE), the Senate approved a bill fixing the term of barangay and SK to five years, effectively postponing the elections again.

On Monday, September 14, 13 senators voted to approve Senate Bill (SB) No. 2387 on third and final reading, while five others — Senate President Pro Tempore Vicente “Tito” Sotto III, and Senators Risa Hontiveros, Bam Aquino, Kiko Pangilinan, and Joel Villanueva — voted against it.
No senator abstained.

Authored by Senator Chiz Escudero, SB No. 2387 seeks to amend Republic Act (RA) No. 12232 by fixing the term of all elected barangay and SK officials from four to five years. It also sets a two-term limit for barangay officials and one term for SK officials.
The bill resets the November 2, 2026 BSKE to the second Monday of November 2028, and subsequent elections to every five years thereafter.
What does this mean for incumbent officials?

Once enacted, SK officials would continue serving in holdover positions, unless they are suspended or removed from office. In case of vacancy, it provides that the rule of succession will prevail for SK chairmanships while mayors are authorized to appoint SK councilors to fill the vacant seats.

The terms of incumbent barangay officials, meanwhile, would be extended to two more years, deeming them to have completed one term in their respective positions. Those who are serving their last or third consecutive term would then be considered ineligible to run for the same post in the 2028 November BSKE.

Sotto, who strongly opposed the passage of the bill, said suspending the polls may violate the voters’ right to suffrage. He also pointed out that fixing the terms of office of barangay officials may be done without amending the law.

“Are we not violating the citizenry’s right of suffrage by denying voters to choose their local leaders?…Fixing the terms of our barangay officials to five years, must be balanced with the interest of the voting public to elect a new mandate… I hope that the November 2026 elections will push through and just apply the new fixed term prospectively if possible,” said Sotto.
The House of Representatives approved its version of the bill on September 8. Fast-tracking its passage, the lower chamber adopted the Senate version of the measure on Wednesday, September 16.

After hurdling Congress, it is now in the hands of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. whether to approve or veto the bill. It may also lapse into law should he decide not to act on it within 30 days of receipt.
The last BSKE was held in November 2023. The next elections was initially scheduled for November 2025 but Marcos Jr. enacted a law moving the local elections to November 2026.

The Commission on Elections (Comelec) previously said it will continue its preparations for the BSKE amid proposals for its postponement. The poll body also said it will abide by the Congress’ decision whether or not to push through with the elections.
Some election watchdogs including Legal Network for Truthful Election (LENTE) and National Citizens’ Movement for Free Elections (NAMFREL) expressed opposition to the postponement.

“The long-term costs of delay outweigh the short-term savings. Fiscal relief from postponing one election cycle is temporary and one-time; the erosion of institutional stability, voter trust, and local accountability that repeated postponements produce is cumulative and lasting,” said NAMFREL.

“A government that keeps the electoral calendar predictable earns more durable public confidence — and more durable cooperation from citizens on economic recovery — than one that keeps moving the goalposts,” it added. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Marcoleta says no furlough bid for impeachment threshold vote
articles.summary: The detained senator insists the impeachment threshold is already in the Constitution.

blocks.text: September 17, 2026 | 3:14pm
Senator Rodante Marcoleta boards a Philippine National Police coaster at the Sandiganbayan on Monday, July 6, 2026, upon his arrest over a plunder case.
The STAR / Michael Varcas

MANILA, Philippines — Detained Sen. Rodante Marcoleta vowed not not seek furlough from the Sandiganbayan to vote on a proposed change to the 16-vote threshold required for conviction in Vice President Sara Duterte's impeachment trial.

At a press conference following the hearing of his plunder case on Monday, September 16, Marcoleta argued that the 16-vote threshold should not be subject to a vote because it is already in the Constitution.
"I will not move for a furlough just to vote for a threshold," Marcoleta said. He was with Mike Defensor, a former lawmaker and detainee, at the event.
"I don't think the threshold is a subject of votation. It's already in the Constitution," he added.
The lawmaker also expressed disappointment that his Senate colleagues did not take up his July 20 manifestation on his participation in the impeachment trial.
His manifestation, according to Marcoleta, also contained questions on the legitimacy of Sen. Francis Escudero as presiding officer and concerning the 16-vote threshold.
"Kung 'di nila (Senate) ite-take up 'yon [manifestation], bakit pa ako makikipag-participate doon?" Marcoleta said.
(If they [the Senate] aren't going to take that up [the manifestation], why should I still participate in it?).
On September 16, three former Supreme Court chief justices, acting as "amici curiae," explained that the Constitution does not fix the number at 16 to convict an official in an impeachment trial.

According to retired magistrates invited to the Senate court, a conviction requires two-thirds of "all the Members of the Senate," but "all" should be interpreted as all qualified, participating members, not necessarily the full 24 if some are legally or physically unable to participate.
Questions about the conviction threshold arose following concerns raised by senator-judges over the applicable vote requirement, considering the Senate's incomplete membership.
This is due to the imprisonment of two senators, Marcoleta and Sen. Jinggoy Estrada, for plunder, and Sen. Bato Dela Rosa being at large due to an International Criminal Court warrant of arrest.

articles.title: Saint, sinner or feminist icon: How Mary Magdalene's image evolved through time
articles.summary: From "Apostle of the Apostles" to prostitute, Mary Magdalene has been assigned a wide variety of roles, as a new exhibition shows.

image.caption: 'Mary Magdalene Mourns at the Body of Christ' by Arnold Böcklin (1867), currently on view at the Städel Museum in FrankfurtImage: Staedel Museum

blocks.text: Apostle, prostitute, penitent and confidante of Jesus — just a few of the roles assigned to Mary Magdalene since the early days of Christianity.

Artists from the Renaissance to the Baroque period, including Titian, El Greco and Georges de la Tour, depicted her in the 16th and 17th centuries as a repentant penitent; Rembrandt portrayed her as a witness to Christ's resurrection; and Max Beckmann, a representative of the New Objectivity movement, depicted her as a sinner in 1917.
Nearly a century later, she was portrayed by Lady Gaga in a music video.

"Mary Magdalene is probably the most multifaceted and enigmatic figure in the Bible, and also one of the most enigmatic in European cultural history," says Bastian Eclercy, curator of the exhibition "Mary Magdalene: Sin. Pray. Love" at the Städel Museum in Frankfurt. "She appears countless times in art history."
What do we know about Mary Magdalene?
Very little is known about Mary Magdalene from the Bible, yet she plays an important role in the New Testament.

The Gospels recount that Jesus delivered her from seven demons, and that she accompanied Jesus and witnessed his crucifixion and burial. On Easter morning, she discovered the empty tomb and became the first witness to the Resurrection. She then proclaimed the message of the risen Christ to Jesus' disciples: "She is then referred to as the Apostula Apostulorum, that is, the Apostle of the Apostles," explains Bastian Eclercy. "This gives her a very central role in the history of salvation."
But it didn't stop there.

blocks.caption: Max Beckmann, 'Christ and the Sinner' (1917)Image: Bequest of Curt Valentin

blocks.text: Around 600 AD, Pope Gregory the Great permanently distorted the image of Mary Magdalene by merging her with two other women mentioned in the Bible: an unnamed woman, the "sinner" mentioned in the Gospel of Luke who washed Christ's feet, and Mary of Bethany (who also washed his feet). The Pope claimed that the seven demons cast out of Mary Magdalene by Jesus represented the seven deadly sins. His sermon played a decisive role in shaping Mary Magdalene's reputation as a repentant prostitute — something for which there is absolutely no evidence in the Bible.
Mary Magdalene's remains are in France — allegedly

In the High Middle Ages, a legend emerged to the effect that Mary Magdalene, together with Lazarus and a group of companions, had been cast adrift in a boat on the Mediterranean; with divine help, she is said to have reached the coast of Provence in France, where she first preached the Gospel and then lived in a cave for some 30 years, doing penance.
Even today, two French towns claim to hold her remains: Vezelay in Burgundy and Saint-Maximin-la-Sainte-Baume in Provence.

blocks.caption: Flushed cheeks, parted lips, an ecstatic gaze: The depiction of Mary Magdalene as a penitent sinner often had an erotic element as well. Painting by Titian, 'The Penitent Mary Magdalene' (c. 1555–1565)Image: Heritage Images/picture alliance

blocks.text: In the 16th century, finally, the Reformation and Renaissance humanism brought about a change in thinking and opposition to the conflation of the three women into one.

However, it was not until the Second Vatican Council (1962 to 1965), which adopted far-reaching reforms to the Roman Catholic liturgy, that the identification of Mary Magdalene with the anonymous sinner was officially revoked.

"This very broad range of roles, which have been attributed to her throughout history and which are in a certain state of tension with one another, has evidently held a particular fascination for artists of all eras and genres time and again, whilst also presenting them with a challenge," explains Bastian Eclercy.

blocks.caption: El Greco, 'The Penitent Mary Magdalene,' c. 1580–1585Image: Worcester Art Museum/Bridgeman Images

blocks.text: A new image through the Gospel of Mary
With the rediscovery of the Gospel of Mary in modern times, the image of Mary Magdalene got something of a makeover.
This text, not included in the biblical canon, portrays her as a particularly close confidante of Jesus and has given fresh impetus to discussions about her role.

Today, she is regarded as one of the most influential women of early Christianity and a key figure in feminist theology. "In recent decades in particular, she has thus become a role model for women — that is, for female observers — but also, and especially, for contemporary female artists, who see in her the qualities of a woman who lives on her own terms," says Eclercy.
Lady Gaga portrayed Mary Magdalene in her 2011 video for "Judas" — "the most exciting artistic moment of my career," as she wrote on Twitter at the time.

The most recent portrait in the Frankfurt exhibition — which features more than 100 depictions of Mary Magdalene — is by the Spanish artist Nieves Gonzalez and was completed in 2025: "La Sfida" (The Challenge) deconstructs virtually all the traditional attributes ascribed to Mary Magdalene by artists of earlier centuries.

blocks.caption: A confident Mary Magdalene in a flashy red coat: 'La sfida' (The Challenge) by Nieves Gonzalez, 2025Image: Nieves González

blocks.text: Where she once gazed penitently towards the heavens, the painting depicts the female apostle looking down at the viewer with a self-assured gaze. Where her hair would otherwise have hung loose — alluding to the figure's sinful past — here it lies carefully brushed around her neck like a scarf. And where much bare skin would normally be visible, her body is now wrapped in a thick red down coat. In her hands, the disciple holds an equally (blood-) red skull — for centuries a symbol of transience — a gesture that clearly expresses her power.

Mary Magdalene has now also been officially recognized as an equal within the Catholic Church: In 2016, Pope Francis elevated her liturgical celebration on July 22 from a Memorial to a Feast, thereby aligning her legal and ritual status with that of male apostles within the faith. It's yet another chapter in the illustrious life story of Mary Magdalene, and unlikely to be the last.
The exhibition "Mary Magdalene: Sin. Pray. Love." runs at the Städel Museum in Frankfurt from September 17 through January 17, 2027.
This article was originally written in German.

articles.title: Escape through drone in Bilibid, jail facilities? No chance, says BuCor's Catapang
articles.summary: Bureau of Corrections (BuCor) Director General Gregorio Catapang Jr. on Thursday ruled out the possibility of persons deprived of liberty (PDLs) escaping through drones, amid viral posts that a South…

blocks.text: Published September 17, 2026 3:01pm

Bureau of Corrections (BuCor) Director General Gregorio Catapang Jr. on Thursday ruled out the possibility of persons deprived of liberty (PDLs) escaping through drones, amid viral posts that a South Korean national planned to escape through such a method.
Catapang issued the statement when asked about the possible use of drones in prison operations, particularly in connection with escape attempts, among others.

“All our Operating Prison and Penal Farms are no-fly zones, and we have watchtowers manned 24/7 which immediately alert our guards if there will be attempts to escape through drones aside from maingay ang drone at equipped naman ang ating facilities ng mga CCTV, so we can detect it at once,” he said.

(All our Operating Prison and Penal Farms are no-fly zones, and we have watchtowers manned 24/7, which immediately alert our guards if there are attempts to escape through drones. Aside from drones being noisy, our facilities are also equipped with CCTV, so we can detect it at once.)
He added that drones cannot operate near the correctional facilities without attracting the attention of prison personnel and security systems.
Meanwhile, he also said that various CCTV cameras throughout correctional facilities allow personnel to monitor prison grounds.
South Korean media reported that Park Wang-yeol planned to escape from prison a month before his extradition in March. However, it reported that his plan fell through.
Meanwhile, Justice Undersecretary Ian Norman Dato said that Parks has been extradited and is now under the custody of the Korean government.
Dato also said that the Department of Justice (DOJ) is confident that BuCor is fully equipped to prevent such incidents.
“The DOJ is confident that our BuCor is fully equipped and prepared to prevent any such eventuality,” he said. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: FACT CHECK: INC rally misrepresented as protest against VP Sara arrest warrant
articles.summary: The video shows a commotion between police and members of the Iglesia ni Cristo during a June 2026 protest in support of Senator Rodante Marcoleta

blocks.text: Claim: A video shows a commotion breaking out between a crowd and the police following an arrest order for Vice President Sara Duterte.

Why we fact-checked this: The post bearing the claim has already received 61,000 views, 205 shares, and 123 comments as of writing. It was posted on September 8, days after the Vice President posted bail for her grave threats case at the Quezon City Regional Trial Court (RTC).

The video shows a commotion between protesters and policemen. Text overlaid on the Facebook reel reads, “Sabi niyo magagalit ang taong bayan pag di natuloy ang impeachment! Bakit nagkakagulo nung inaresto niyo si VP? Nagkamali kayo ng ginalaw!”
(You said the public would be outraged if the impeachment didn’t push through! So why was there an uproar when you arrested the VP? You messed with the wrong person!)

Several Facebook users believed that the protest shown in the video was indeed a rally against Duterte’s arrest. One comment reads, “[Sige] pa nakakagigil talaga sarap sumali [dyan] ah laban mga kabayan (Keep it up! It’s truly exciting. It would be great to join in on that. Fight on, fellow citizens).”

The facts: The video does not show a recent rally held to oppose the arrest warrant against Duterte. It shows a commotion between the police and members of the Iglesia ni Cristo during the “surprise” protest on June 30 in support of their fellow INC member, Senator Rodante Marcoleta, who was facing a possible arrest at the time.

Although covered by superimposed text, certain landmarks such as the Primex Tower, J&L Building, and the Midway Court Building can still be seen in the video. These buildings are located along EDSA. A commotion between police officers and INC protesters was reported around this site on June 30.

A video posted by ANC 24/7 matches the location of the clash between INC members and uniformed personnel. Establishments in the Midway Court Building such as the Dojo Garage and Vertiflute can be seen in the video. GMA News also reported the commotion on June 30, showing similar scenes of the INC protest.

The misleading Facebook reel misrepresented the INC rally as a protest against Duterte’s arrest warrant. While several supporters gathered at the Quezon City court on September 5 and on September 11 to show support for Duterte ahead of her arraignment, the crowd was smaller than those shown in the INC rally footage.
Arrest warrant: On September 4, the Quezon City RTC Branch 98 issued a warrant of arrest against Duterte in connection with her grave threats case.

The case, filed by the Department of Justice last August, stemmed from Duterte’s alleged threat to assassinate President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, and former House speaker Martin Romualdez, based on her statements during a November 2024 online press briefing.
On September 5, the Vice President posted a P360,000 bail on for all three counts.
Previous fact checks: Rappler has previously fact-checked similar misrepresented rallies:

items: FACT CHECK: Nepal protest, Trillion Peso March misrepresented as recent rallies in PHFACT CHECK: Video of Peñafrancia procession misrepresented as rally in Metro Manila
FACT CHECK: Videos of La Naval procession, Nepal protests misrepresented as rallies in PH
FACT CHECK: Video of rally calling for Marcos’ resignation is AI-generated
FACT CHECK: Concert photo misrepresented as Duterte prayer rally crowd in Cebu
FACT CHECK: Video of 2024 Cebu concert misrepresented as Duterte rally crowd
FACT CHECK: No clash between protesters, police in Liwasang Bonifacio rally

blocks.text: – Angelee Kaye Abelinde/Rappler.com
Angelee Kaye Abelinde is a student journalist based in Naga City, and an alumna of Rappler’s Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship 2024.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

articles.title: North-south Commuter Railway full operation timeline revised to 2033
articles.summary: North-south Commuter Railway full operation timeline revised to 2033

blocks.text: Published September 17, 2026 2:59pm
The timeline of completion for the North-south Commuter Railway (NSCR) has been revised, with complete operations being eyed by 2033, according to Malacañang.
The NSCR, a 147.26-kilometer elevated railway linking Central Luzon, Metro Manila and Calabarzon, was expected to be finished by 2032.
However, Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said that following the 11th Economy and Development Council Meeting, the timeline has been moved due to budgetary constraints.

“Nagkaroon po ng kaunting pagbabago tungkol sa timeline, dahil alam naman po natin na nagkaroon ng medyo pagtitipid, mag-iingat sa pondo ng bayan at nahirapan po sa mga procurements and maliban pa po diyan ay nagkakaroon din po ng isyu sa right of way,” Castro said.

(There is a slight change in the timeline, because we know that there has been a bit of cost-cutting, being cautious of public funds and there was a difficulty in procurement and other than that, there was also an issue with the right of way.)
According to Castro, the new timeline will be as follows:

items: December 2027 - First partial operation from Valenzuela to Malolos
Fourth quarter of 2028 - Second partial operation from Malolos to Clark
Fourth quarter of 2031 - Third partial operation from Clark-Solis, Alabang to Calamba
Third quarter of 2033 - Full operation from Clark to Calamba

blocks.text: “Usually po ang mga amendments nito ay iyong mga timelines lang po at medyo may pag-aadjust din po ng kaunti sa budget,” Castro said.
(Usually, these amendments in the timeline will also have an adjusted budget.) —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: Abducted South African journalist found dead with gunshot wounds
articles.summary: The body of veteran broadcaster Owen Ndlovu was found hours after armed men kidnapped him near Johannesburg.

blocks.text: Provincial police spokesperson Col Dimakatso Nevhuhulwi said Ndlovu had gone to pick up his wife from a religious service when the attackers struck.
"As she approached their vehicle, three unknown men, one reportedly armed with a firearm, suddenly approached them, pushed her aside and forced her husband into the back seat," she said.
"The suspects then drove off with the victim."
The vehicle, a Ford Raptor pick-up truck - commonly known as a bakkie in South Africa - was later recovered abandoned in Walkerville, an area south of Johannesburg, police said.
Ndlovu's body was found by local residents beside a road in Thokoza, which neighbours Katlehong. They said he appeared to have suffered gunshot wounds.
A bag of his was found a few metres away.
Police said they were investigating a case of murder but a post-mortem examination would establish the cause of death.
"At this stage, the family is awaiting further information from the relevant authorities regarding the circumstances surrounding Owen's death," said family spokesperson Eugene Mthethwa.
The family described the loss as "devastating" and thanked residents, police and members of the public who had helped search for him after news of his abduction emerged.
Ndlovu was a familiar figure to South African sports fans after years working as a presenter and producer at the SABC.
He was also involved in radio coverage of the country's Premier Soccer League and later became an advocate for musicians' rights and royalty payments.
The 54-year-old was also associated with Artists United and the SABC Summer Song of the Year initiative.
Lelo Mzaca, a fellow journalist, remembered him as a man who lived a "colourful, energetic life" and brought enthusiasm and flair to sports broadcasting.
"South Africa has lost a unique and spirited individual whose light shone brightly while it lasted," Mzaca added in a tribute on the Mail & Guardian news site.
The provincial government urged communities to help police with the investigation, saying tackling crime remained a priority.
The killing has again drawn attention to violent crime in South Africa, where armed robberies and vehicle hijackings remain a major concern.
The latest national police figures, covering April to June 2026, recorded more than 5,000 murders and close to 4,000 carjackings.

When releasing the figures last month, acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia said serious crimes continued to create fear in communities and that some were carried out by "organised, heavily armed criminal groups that operate with planning and sophistication".

articles.title: Australia Post worker stole dozens of bank cards to fund ‘debilitating’ gambling addiction
articles.summary:
Court hears Mauro Paul Coluzzi and two associates defrauded customers and banks of more than $130,000

An Australia Post worker’s crippling gambling addiction spiralled into purchases of gold…

blocks.text: An Australia Post worker’s crippling gambling addiction spiralled into purchases of gold jewellery, phones and even online gaming gift cards with stolen bank cards.
Mauro Paul Coluzzi’s family members broke down in court as he was jailed until December 2027 for leading two criminal syndicates funded with pilfered plastic.
The disgraced postal worker, 57, stole dozens of cards out of secure mail on his beat in Sydney’s eastern suburbs.
Over 15 months, Coluzzi and two co-conspirators defrauded customers and their banks of more than $100,000.
The postie personally obtained nearly $30,000 in cash and goods from the stolen cards, including two 24-carat gold bracelets bought 12 hours before his arrest.
Coluzzi reduced community confidence in the reliability of the postal service and prison time was a must, judge Jillian Kiely found.
“(Cards) were stolen from the post which was a significant breach of trust … to safely deliver these items to customers,” she said in Sydney’s Sutherland local court on Thursday.
An unblemished postal worker since 2007, Coluzzi began looking for new ways to fund a debilitating gambling addiction in early 2024, Kiely said.
“I hope they all work, I need money bro,” Coluzzi told one of his co-offenders.
“I’m fucked bro, I gotta pay my credit card.”
The agreed facts of the case state that, by the end of the scheme, Coluzzi was worried about changes to Australia Post procedures that would stop him from accessing new cards.
“It’s only gonna be parcels bro, and I can’t fucking touch parcels,” he said to an unnamed person.
Australia Post has zero tolerance for illegal activity in its network, a spokesperson said.
“We worked very closely with NSW Police throughout their investigation and continually review systems and processes to strengthen the security of our operations.”
Coluzzi is estimated to have gambled millions of dollars throughout his life and the excessive losses put repeated strain on his marriage, Kiely said.
after newsletter promotion
For 15 months, the Australia Post employee and his accomplices systematically stole dozens of cards from secure mail and obtained more than $100,000 in cash and fraudulent purchases.
The men bought perfume, a night out in Darling Harbour, scented candles and more than a dozen phones and tablets.
Thousands of cigarettes, phone recharge cards, groceries and Roblox gift cards were also in the haul.
Coluzzi’s barrister, Troy Edwards SC, argued a community sentence would be an appropriate punishment for the 57-year-old.
But Kiely said the offending was too serious for any sentence but jail.
As Coluzzi was led away by sheriff’s officers from the court, a member of his family collapsed and had to be assisted from the court.
He will be eligible for parole in December 2027.

articles.title: US extends visa denial for Palestinian officials ahead of UNGA
articles.summary: The US State Department extended its visa sanctions on Palestinian officials, ahead of the UN General Assembly. Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas will likely submit a video statement for…

image.caption: AFP reported that the US State Department has already denied entry visa to Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud AbbasImage: Yoan Valat/REUTERS

blocks.text: The United States will extend visa sanctions on Palestinian Authority (PA) officials and members of the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO), its State Department said on Wednesday, ahead of the upcoming United Nations General Assembly in New York.

This was "as a consequence of their failure to reform, contrary to their commitments to the United States and their ongoing activities that undermine the prostects for peace," the department said in a statement. The PA and PLO had "once again, failed to live up to their commitments," it added.

The State Department accused the Palestinian Authority and the PLO of taking actions "to internationalize the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, including through the International Criminal Court and International Court of Justice." It also accused the groups of "continuing to pay stipends to terrorists."

Meanwhile, news agency AFP reported that the US had denied Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas an entry visa to attend the UN General Assemblyin New York next week, citing a source familiar with the case.
Why is the Israeli-Palestinian conflict so hard to resolve?
Can the US deny visas to foreign diplomats?

As per a 1947 UN "headquarters agreement," the US is required to allow access for foreign diplomats to the UN Headquarters in New York. However, Washington has said it can deny visas for reasons of security, foreign policy and extremism.
Washington had denied visas to several Palestinians ahead of last years's UN General Assembly as well, and did not allow Abbas to travel to New York.

The US State Department's latest statement comes as the 193-member UN General Assembly is due to vote on Thursday to allow Abbas to submit a video statement for the gathering next week, like he did last year.

The Palestinian Authority, which represents the Palestinian people at the UN, is not a full member and has not vote in the General Assembly. They are an observer state which holds the same status as the Vatican.
However, several UN members including France recognized a Palestinian state at the UN last year.

articles.title: Senators question NIA's P233.85B budget request for 2027
articles.summary: The National Irrigation Administration (NIA) is seeking a P233.85-billion budget for 2027, nearly four times its P64.37-billion allocation for this year, drawing questions from senators.

blocks.text: The National Irrigation Administration (NIA) is seeking a P233.85-billion budget for 2027, nearly four times its P64.37-billion allocation for this year, drawing questions from senators.

During NIA’s budget deliberation at the Senate, Senator Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan highlighted the need to improve the country’s irrigation systems, especially with the expected prolonged drought starting in the last quarter of 2026 due to El Niño.

“Ilang buwan nang nagsasabi ang mga scientists natin sa PAGASA na darating ang napakalakas na El Niño sa huling buwan ng 2026 hanggang sa unang anim na buwan ng 2027. Kaya hindi ngayon ang panahon para magtipid sa kanal, pumps, reservoir, communal irrigation, at pagkukumpuni ng mga irrigation systems,” he said in his opening remarks.

(Our PAGASA scientists have been saying for months that a very strong El Niño will arrive in the last months of 2026 and continue through the first six months of 2027. So now is not the time to skimp on canals, pumps, reservoirs, communal irrigation, and the repair of irrigation systems.)
Pangilinan, however, questioned the large amount being requested by NIA for 2027.
“Bakit kayo humihingi ng napakalaking [budget]? Alam niyo na siguro na hindi aaprubahan,” Pangilinan said.
(Why are you asking for such a huge [budget]? You probably already know that it won't be approved.)
NIA Administrator Eduardo Eddie Guillen said the amount being requested reflects the needs of the agricultural sector.

“Trabaho po kasi natin na ipakita kung anong totoong kailangan ng ating magsasaka. Kayo po nagsabi kanina na mahalaga ang irigasyon. In fact, pwede kang magtanim kahit walang lupa pero hindi ka puwedeng magtanim nang walang tubig,” he said.
(Because it is our job to show what our farmers truly need. You yourself said earlier that irrigation is important. In fact, you can plant even without soil, but you cannot plant without water.)
Senator Imee Marcos also questioned NIA’s requested budget, noting that nearly P17 billion from its current budget remains unutilized.

“Nagtataka lang ako, I'm also perplexed by this huge increase requested, although siyempre gusto natin i-accommodate lahat 'yan dahil kailangan na kailangan with the impending ‘Godzilla’ El Niño. Pero considering na hindi niyo naman nagastos yung 2026 budget. Mayroong halos P17 billion na continuing appropriations, hindi niyo nagastos,” she said.

(I'm just wondering, I'm also perplexed by this huge increase requested, although of course we want to accommodate all of that because it's desperately needed with the impending ‘Godzilla’ El Niño. But considering that you haven't even spent your 2026 budget, there is almost P17 billion in continuing appropriations that you haven't spent.)

Guillen explained that the requested budget also reflects requests made by Regional Development Councils (RDCs). He added that NIA can manage with whatever amount is ultimately approved for the agency.

“Isang ni-reflect natin diyan ay yung sa RDC request. So sinala natin yung RDC request, tinanggalan na natin at we came up with the [P233 billion]. So ang trabaho natin ipakita natin yung pangangailangan at request. Of course, kaya naman po natin kung ano po yung merong budget ay yun po yung i-implement natin. It's just that kailangan namin ipakita yung totoong sitwasyon,” Guillen said.

(One of the things we reflected there is the RDC request. So we filtered the RDC requests, trimmed them down, and came up with [P233 billion]. Our job is to show the needs and requests. Of course, we can manage—whatever budget is available, that's what we will implement. It's just that we need to show the real situation.)
The senators also questioned NIA’s requested P1.7-billion quick response fund, which is significantly higher than the P300 million allocated for the fund in 2026.
“Saksakan ng laki ito. Gusto namin malaman what disaster risks are you intending to cover? Ano bang plano diyan at napakalaki?” Marcos asked.
(This is extremely large. We want to know what disaster risks you intend to cover. What is the plan that requires such a large amount?)
Guillen said the amount would help NIA prepare for the expected Super El Niño.
“Paparating po ang Super El Niño, eh palagay ko yung tig-P100 million per region na lamang ay baka kulang po sa P1.7 billion,” he said.
(Super El Niño is coming, and I think even P100 million per region may not be enough compared with the P1.7 billion.)
State weather bureau PAGASA has warned that El Niño could strengthen in the latter part of 2026.
Its possible impacts include below-normal rainfall, prolonged dry conditions, and drought in parts of the Philippines, potentially affecting agriculture and water resources. —VBL, GMA News

articles.title: DOE scraps coal bid, plans rebid in weeks as Semirara contract nears expiry
articles.summary: ‘We’ll rebid in a few weeks. New rules, new bidding,’ Energy Secretary Sharon Garin tells Rappler as Semirara’s contract nears its July 2027 expiry

blocks.text: ‘We’ll rebid in a few weeks. New rules, new bidding,’ Energy Secretary Sharon Garin tells Rappler as Semirara’s contract nears its July 2027 expiry

MANILA, Philippines – The Department of Energy (DOE) scrapped its 2026 coal bid round but plans to launch a new auction within weeks, resetting the race for the country’s biggest coal-producing area less than a year before the existing contract of Semirara Mining and Power Corporation (SMPC) expires.
In an advisory on Tuesday, September 15, Energy Secretary Sharon Garin terminated the bidding covering three pre-determined areas offered for development and production coal operating contracts.

The DOE cited concerns raised during pre-submission conferences, as well as developments affecting Semirara Island in Antique province, including “continuing water seepage” and unspecified “legal considerations.”

“We’ll rebid in a few weeks,” Garin told Rappler when asked whether terminating the auction this close to SMPC’s contract expiration could make it harder for another operator to prepare for a takeover.
“New rules, new bidding,” she added on Thursday, September 17.

blocks.caption: Image from Department of Energy

blocks.text: In its advisory, the department said the termination would allow it to develop a “fair, equitable, transparent, and comprehensive evaluation framework,” particularly for areas with confirmed or established coal reserves.

The most consequential part of the aborted auction involves 10 coal blocks on Semirara Island currently operated by Consunji-led SMPC. Its Coal Operating Contract No. 5 expires on July 14, 2027, after the government rejected the company’s bid to extend its decades-long tenure and instead decided to open the area to competition.
The auction has already faced repeated delays. In July, Garin said changes to the bidding rules could be finished within “a few weeks,” according to a BusinessMirror report.

SMPC has also challenged parts of the bidding process in court. In July, it sought protection from DOE demands for detailed asset inventories and proprietary technical information intended to be made available to prospective bidders. – Rappler.com
